title: Exam-day anxiety plan
examples: What is the best breathing exercise to use right before an exam?
How should I approach the first question if I feel really nervous?
Can you give me a quick routine to use in the exam hall?

explain.say: When you feel worried before a test, deep breathing helps calm your body.

items: Step 1: Breathe in slowly through your nose for four counts.
Step 2: Hold your breath gently for a count of two.
Step 3: Breathe out slowly through your mouth for six counts.

draw.text: Deep Breathing: Breathe In, Breathe Out

explain.say: Another helpful technique is to read the whole paper first without writing anything down.

items: Step 1: Look over all the questions on the exam paper.
Step 2: Identify which questions you know best.
Step 3: Plan the order you will answer them in.

draw.text: Strategy: Skim the Whole Paper First

explain.say: For the very first question, try to answer what you know best first.
If you get stuck on a question, it is okay to leave a small space and move on.
In real life, when you are waiting for results, taking deep breaths helps you stay calm.
A common mistake is trying to answer the hardest question first when you feel anxious.

faq.q: Should I breathe when I feel nervous during the test?
faq.a: Yes, taking slow, deep breaths can signal to your brain that you are safe. Try breathing in for four counts and out for six counts.
asks: What breathing exercises work best for exams?
Can deep breathing actually help my nerves?

faq.q: What if I don't know the answer to the first question?
faq.a: Do not spend too much time on one question. If you are stuck, mark the question and move to the next one you feel more confident about.
asks: Is it okay to skip a question?
What should I do if I blank out on the first question?

faq.q: Is it better to read the whole paper or start answering right away?
faq.a: It is best to read the whole paper first. This gives you an overview and helps you plan your time effectively.
asks: Should I read the instructions first?
How long should I spend planning the paper?

faq.q: Does this plan work for all subjects?
faq.a: These are general techniques for managing test anxiety and pacing. You can adapt them for any subject you are studying.
asks: Does this apply to maths exams too?
Are these tips only for written exams?

faq.q: How long before the exam should I practice this plan?
faq.a: Practice these techniques during your revision time, not just the night before. Regular practice makes them automatic.
asks: When should I start practicing this?
How often should I do these breathing exercises?

facts: Deep breathing slows your heart rate and calms your nervous system.
Reading the whole paper first helps you manage your time better.
If you get stuck, moving on and returning later is a good strategy.
Starting with an easier question builds positive momentum.

quiz.say: When you feel very anxious at the start of an exam, what is the best immediate physical action to take?
quiz.show: A. Write down everything you remember.

options.show: A. Writing down everything you remember.
options.say: A. Writing down everything you remember.

options.show: B. Staring at the clock to see how much time is left.
options.say: B. Staring at the clock to see how much time is left.

options.show: C. Asking the teacher for help immediately.
options.say: C. Asking the teacher for help immediately.

options.show: Deep breathing exercises, such as breathing in for four counts and out for six c
options.say: Deep breathing exercises, such as breathing in for four counts and out for six c

quiz.why: This physical action directly calms your body's stress response, allowing your mind to focus.

wrong.0: This can make you feel more pressure to recall everything at once.
wrong.1: Focusing on the clock increases anxiety about time passing.
wrong.2: This uses up valuable time and might draw unwanted attention.

quiz.say: You have finished reading the paper and see questions 1, 2, and 5. Which order should you plan to answer them?

options.show: C. The order they are marked in the book.
options.say: C. The order they are marked in the book.

options.show: The order of easiest to hardest, or the order that builds confidence.
options.say: The order of easiest to hardest, or the order that builds confidence.

quiz.why: This strategy ensures you start with a success to build momentum for the harder questions.

wrong.0: You should prioritize confidence building over simply reversing the order.
wrong.1: The book order does not reflect the difficulty level of the questions.
wrong.3: This forces you to tackle the questions in a potentially difficult sequence.

quiz.say: If you get stuck on a question, what is the best next step according to the plan?
quiz.show: A. Keep staring at the question until the answer appears.

options.show: B. Erasing your previous answers repeatedly.
options.say: B. Erasing your previous answers repeatedly.

options.show: C. Asking a friend sitting nearby for help.
options.say: C. Asking a friend sitting nearby for help.

options.show: Mark the question and move on to a different topic or question.
options.say: Mark the question and move on to a different topic or question.

options.show: A. Keep staring at the question until the answer appears.
options.say: A. Keep staring at the question until the answer appears.

quiz.why: This prevents you from wasting valuable time on one difficult point.

wrong.0: This action does not help and wastes time you could use elsewhere.
wrong.1: This is not allowed in the exam setting and does not help you learn.
wrong.3: Staring often increases the feeling of panic and blocks thinking.
